source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), General Directorate of Agriculture, Department of Agricultural Extension — 'បច្ចេកទេសដាំដំណាំឪឡឹក' (Watermelon Cultivation Techniques), 2017.
text:
Watermelon requires regular watering, and irrigation needs increase as the plant grows larger and as weather becomes hotter — the crop needs closer attention to watering during hot periods. Farmers should water regularly according to the season: watering can generally be less frequent during the cool/rainy season, but during the hot season, if the weather is very hot and dry, farmers may need to water more than once a day (both morning and evening as needed).

Irrigation water should not be applied directly onto the plant's growing crown/central stem, since this can cause the crown to rot; water should be applied around the root zone instead. If the field uses furrow irrigation (flooding the furrows between beds), care should be taken to not let water rise onto the top of the bed and reach the base of the plant for too long, as prolonged wetness at the stem base can promote crown and stem-rot disease.
